reason: A is the better proposal because it directly compares chloride corrosion at room temperature and the specified 700–900 °C regime, with film-quality controls and time-resolved measurements tied to breakdown and secondary-scale formation. Although its predictions are overly noncommittal and partly restate prior room-temperature work, B’s 60 °C concrete-pore test is not a valid proxy for 700–900 °C hot corrosion, making its cross-regime mechanism and claimed annealing benefit physically unsupported.
